conserved_row.complete_before_row: 7.1 The implication $\epsilon=0\Rightarrow\tau=0$ uses the normalized horizontal homology supplied by [F2]. Set $s=\tau$ and use $G_s\ne0$ to choose a Maslov-zero southwest-hook cycle $y=z+\ell$ mapping to the normalized vertical class, where $z$ is on the lower vertical ray and $\ell$ is strictly left at $j=s$. Homogeneity is available by projecting a preimage to Maslov degree zero. Its horizontal projection $h=z_c+\ell$, with $z_c$ its corner part, is a horizontal cycle. If it were a horizontal boundary, write a bounding chain as $a_++a_-$, splitting strictly right support from support at $i\le0$. The right component of its boundary is zero; the corner is $z_c=(\partial a_+)_c+(\partial a_-)_c$. In the northeast hook, the chain $a_++(a_-)_c$ then has boundary exactly $z_c$: the left part of $a_-$ cannot reach the corner, and differential from the corner toward the left is killed in that hook. But $F_s([z])$ is represented by $z_c$, so this would give $F_s=0$, contrary to $\epsilon=0$. Thus $h$ is a nonzero horizontal homology class in Maslov degree zero. Multiplication by $U^s$ takes it to horizontal level zero and Maslov degree $-2s$. Actual normalized conjugation [F2] identifies that horizontal homology with the vertical homology generated in Maslov degree zero, giving $s=0$. The geometric conjugation and absolute normalization used here are supplied by [F2]; thus this implication no longer has a separate conjugation hold. [given, F1, F2, construct, algebra] ∎

conserved_row.complete_before_row: 3.1 Work in the TOP group of [F8]. Fix $n\ge1$ and any desired finite rank $m$. Choose the finite family in [F6] for size $m+1$. If a nonzero signed sum of its $P^n$ iterates belonged to $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}$, its defining TOP solution would have exactly the integral height-$n$ pairs and isotropic height-$(n+1)$ lifts needed by [F5]. The finite forest quotient maps in [F5] have amenable target in the specified $D(k)$ class, with top meridian of infinite order. The accepted TOP half-pair theorem gives zero defect of that actual solution; the smooth standard joining/infection pieces have zero defect as well. Whole-component additivity makes the actual boundary defect sum zero. But [F6] evaluates its bottom terms by canonical cyclic numbers and gives strict signed domination over all pattern terms. This is a contradiction. Thus these $m+1$ classes are rationally independent modulo $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}$: a rational relation clears denominators to the excluded nonzero signed integer relation.
